about: Rows of docs/research/baggage-claims-content-proposal.csv that state one of the owner's documents plainly and need no decision from him (his ruling of 22 Nov 2026, option B). Each row names the sheet row it comes from and the document and place it was checked against. Rows are added once per database by src/lib/seedContentDb.ts; a row a person has changed is left alone.

rows.title: Stakeholder: traveler (buyer)
rows.body: Pain: airports are stressful, anonymous, boring. Relief: turns dead travel time into a shared joke at weigh-in, belt and carousel.

rows.title: Stakeholder: gift-giver
rows.body: Pain: needs a $20-30 gift that is NOT another candle. Relief: instant novelty; gag price band proven at $12-15 on Etsy and eBay.

rows.title: Stakeholder: baggage handler and bystander
rows.body: Pain: invisible labor. Relief: the bag talks back; handlers become the audience and the viral content engine.

rows.title: Stakeholder: retailer
rows.body: Pain: the gag shelf churns on meme cycles. Relief: seasonal voice packs refresh the SKU without new hardware.

rows.title: Data flow and firmware states
rows.body: IMU 100 Hz > ring buffer > feature extractor > state machine (BOOT / CALIBRATE / IDLE / ACTIVE_SAMPLE / CLASSIFY / DISPATCH / COOLDOWN) > UART > DFPlayer > 8-ohm speaker. Single-board device, radios disabled.

rows.title: Realistic ceiling
rows.body: "The realistic ceiling on a single gag run is a viral 5-figure-to-low-6-figure seasonal product", and the worst case is "the funniest road-trip companion ever made".

rows.title: Scale or exit
rows.body: Phase 3 always-on: TikTok Shop and Shopify DTC; an Amazon listing tuned to gag travel gift keywords; an airport gift-store wholesale pitch with a counter display playing one clip on button-press; holiday voice packs as the re-purchase hook; luggage-brand licensing (co-brand) as the scale-or-exit option.

rows.title: Success metrics: product and business
rows.body: Product: idle false positives under 1 a day, return rate under 4%, 4.3+ stars. Business: 45% blended gross margin on the first production run; 20% of buyers attach a DLC voice pack within 12 months.

rows.appendBody: Each segment's signal and job. P1 frequent leisure flyers 25-45: core gifting demographic; express personality, prank travel companions, TikTokable moments. P2 gag-gift buyers (Secret Santa, Father's Day): Q4 gifting spike; a $20-30 stocking-stuffer with an explanation-free 90-second demo. P3 travel content creators: high leverage, low price sensitivity; a prop that generates clips, affiliate partners. P4 airport gift shops and novelty retail: Paradies/Hudson-style channel; high-margin impulse checkout SKU.

The PRD's detail: (1) the trigger-pattern classifier is "hard to copy well without flying duffel bags around"; (3) the alkaline trick rests on FAA PackSafe (lithium devices must be fully OFF in the hold). From the risk table: the classifier is treated as a trade secret, alongside a design patent and trademark.

Generate the Arduino sketch for the classification.md
rows.appendBody: One gag per event class per journey phase; in the sketch a new journey phase begins after 60 minutes without motion (PHASE_RESET_MS), which clears every class latch. A gag is refused while the player's BUSY line is low, within 3 s of the last gag, or after 6 in the rolling hour (serial log "GOV: cap, refused"). The volume button is usable between clips only.

Short press cycles volume 50 / 75 / 100%, sent as player volume 15 / 23 / 30; the sketch starts at 23. Long press swaps the voice pack (sketch: held over 1.5 s; packs 1 to 3 in turn). A 10 s hold is a factory reset (sketch: over 9 s, restarts the processor). Active low with a 10k pull-up, debounce 30 ms in software. The button must be reachable through a slot in the shell.

rows.title: Feature extraction
rows.body: From the 100 Hz samples the firmware derives magnitude, jerk, variance, orientation and periodicity (design package); the PRD lists magnitude, jerk, tilt and gravity-removed axes, with variance windows of 0.5 s and 8 s.

rows.title: Audio command interface
rows.body: UART 9600 8N1, YX5200 command set (0x7E frame). Set volume: 0x06 v (0-30). Play folder file: 0x0F f i, where f is the voice pack (1-3) and i the gag index (1-128). Playback status: BUSY on GPIO4, LOW while playing; the dispatcher holds its queue.

rows.title: Loudness limit
rows.body: No more than 85 dBA at 1 m, "to stay a novelty, not a nuisance". 3 W into 8 ohms. No measurement method is given.

rows.title: Radios off
rows.body: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth are disabled in firmware, to save power and to keep the device out of RF certification scope; no networking.

rows.title: Rigid sensor mount
rows.body: U2 must be screwed down through its two holes, never foam mounted: "Mounting compliance destroys jerk signatures." In a flexible TPU case the sensor is screwed to a rigid internal sled, not to the case.

rows.title: Service and debug port
rows.body: USB-C on the dev board (IF-7) for flashing and a 115200 baud debug console. The serial log prints one "EVT:" line per classifier firing, with pack and clip, and doubles as the tuning log.

rows.title: Content ships independently of firmware
rows.body: Clips swap per voice pack, so seasonal editions, DLC and localization need no new hardware and no firmware change; a pack is a folder of numbered files on the card.

rows.title: Idle false positives under one a day
rows.body: Product metric and Rev A1 exit criterion: fewer than one false gag a day while idle. No test method is given.

rows.appendBody: The design package's check: with the switch open VIN reads 0 V, closed about 4.7 V. Never battery-power the board while USB-C is inserted (boot loop).
4.7k pull-ups are on the GY-521 board, so none are added. Digital 3.3 V.
The design package's check: never connect GND to VCC; the MPU-6050 board's LED is lit when powered.
Carries status and ACK frames.
LOW while playing; gates the dispatcher. If it floats, sleep current is high (troubleshooting).
Differential drive from SPK_1 / SPK_2, 8 ohm, no more than 3 W (interface IF-4); route the leads down the side wall channel.

rows.title: Tools and materials on the bench
rows.body: Soldering iron and solder, flush cutters, small Phillips screwdriver, tweezers, hot glue, multimeter, USB-C cable, a PC with Arduino IDE 2.x. The design package lists "hot glue or M2 kit" and no tweezers, cable or PC.

rows.title: Threshold tuning on the bench
rows.body: No shake table needed. Put the unit in a duffel bag; drop onto carpet from 0.3, 0.6 and 1.0 m; play a luggage-carousel video loop for the carousel timing; log raw IMU to serial CSV. Tune IMPACT_G and STILL_VAR first: "those two constants gate the two highest-ranked gags in the catalog".

rows.title: Rev A1: threshold tuning on real flights
rows.body: Roadmap step A1, weeks 2-4: tune the thresholds on real flights and record the 128-clip voice-over with a contracted voice actor. Exit: idle false positives under one a day; the "suitcase test suite" passes.

rows.title: Troubleshooting: boot loop
rows.body: Cause: battery and USB both connected. Fix: use one source only.

rows.title: Troubleshooting: no gags, but the log shows events
rows.body: Check the microSD format, the folder names and the file numbering.

rows.title: Troubleshooting: gags at random
rows.body: Cause: the 1 k ohm resistor on the DFPlayer RX line is missing (step 12c).

rows.title: Troubleshooting: weigh-in never fires
rows.body: Cause: U2 is mounted on foam or is loose. Fix: remount it rigidly (step 11).

rows.title: Troubleshooting: high sleep current
rows.body: Cause: the DFPlayer BUSY line is floating. Fix: check step 12e, and that the DFPlayer is idle.

Set the multimeter to continuity; it is used after every solder step. 4. Soldering iron 350 C; never power the board from battery AND USB at once.

rows.appendBody: Layout target: 5 x 7 cm perfboard, components on female headers (socketed, not soldered directly, so modules are replaceable).

rows.title: Rev D - retail display model
rows.body: Retail display model; voice-pack SD DLC; licensing talks; month 9 onward.

rows.appendBody: Also sold as a Kickstarter add-on at checkout and in the cart on the product page; stretch-goal packs cost "$0.50/unit to fulfill"; registering a unit gives the first pack free. Target: 20% of buyers attach at least one pack within 12 months.

rows.title: Margin targets
rows.body: Target blended margin 45% at launch, "expanding past 55% on repeat batches as COGS compresses and DLC voice packs ... attach". The PRD's margins by channel at $11.15: Kickstarter early bird 35%, Kickstarter standard 49%, DTC 49%, Amazon FBA 43%, wholesale 23%.

rows.title: The video is the business plan
rows.body: The product's demonstration is its marketing. "This video is the business plan" (first proposal); "our entire marketing asset IS the demo video" (PRD); "Content cost: near-zero - every unit in the wild is a content generator" (PRD).

rows.appendBody: The production rules from the script: the hero voice is the final contracted talent, not scratch; "never fake the AUDIO"; keep the device visible in frame in at least 4 shots ("backers fund what they can see"); the on-screen supers name the real firmware event classes so the video doubles as a technical demo. The website's rule: every page masquerades as a piece of airport infrastructure and ends in exactly one conversion action.
